title: Trump admin didn't investigate Jensen Huang before pushing Nvidia to bring him back: 'What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what?'
summary: Nvidia is also not under investigation, according to US Attorney General Todd Blanche.
body: US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he'd given Nvidia "assurance" that ousted and now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang did not represent a national security threat despite an affair with a woman who was reportedly in contact with China's top spy agency. Trump provided that assurance without any formal investigation into Huang's dealings. On whether Huang had been investigated, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said during a press conference this week, "I don't want to talk about investigation. What does that mean, had Huang been investigated? For what? I don't understand the question." Blanche also said that he did not know about any export control investigation related to Nvidia, even though potential violations of export control law are the central concern of the scandal. "A critical national security threat in the Nvidia situation is that Jensen Huang shipped extremely advanced chips to China, violating US export control law, in what amounts to the equivalent of selling rocket engines to the Soviets during the Space Race," Senate minority leader Chuck Schumer said on Tuesday. According to sources speaking to Reuters , Trump's assurance to the Nvidia board was based on …

title: As the US Treasury suffers a cybersecurity breach, its chief tech guy is vibecoding a Civilization clone
summary: The DOGE alum Treasury CIO says his passion project is "so cool."
body: This week, amidst ongoing service disruptions, the US Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it is "investigating a cybersecurity incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." The bureau, which collects and analyzes transaction data to combat financial crimes, says it has taken some of its e-filing systems offline "as a proactive measure." FinCEN hasn't provided an estimate of when the investigation and system disruptions will be resolved, leaving the ability of financial institutions to report suspicious activity and interface with law enforcement indefinitely hampered. Meanwhile, as FinCEN is putting out fires, US Treasury chief information officer Sam Corcos has been busying himself with a different kind of work: He's been vibecoding a Civilization clone. (Image credit: FinCEN) Corcos' LLM-powered game project was noticed by Bulwark economics editor Catherine Rampell: "The Treasury CIO appears to have spent the past three days vibecoding a Civilization game clone instead of working on this major Treasury database cyber breach," she wrote in a post on X . title: AI kills another coding competition: 'I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models'
summary: After eight years of operation, the Atari Homebrew Awards are no more.
body: The Atari Homebrew Awards , an annual celebration of new games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI. "As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums . "Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of new AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs. "The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the new fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I…

title: GTA 6's best lore drops happen when you're chilling with your partner, so stop leaving them at home all the time
summary: Learning things about your partner by spending time with them? Say it ain't so.
body: My real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do. And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments. (Image credit: Rockstar) Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful.…

title: The race to port GTA 6 to PC, explained
summary: GTA 6 could be a PC game (illegally) in a matter of days.
body: Things are moving fast. Now that an illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 is out in the wild, anonymous modders are racing to port it to PC, and the work is progressing faster than many expected. At this rate, it's possible that a static recompilation of GTA 6 will run on a PC in a matter of days. It's also possible it will take much longer to produce a playable build that's actually on par with the console versions. What we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects. As always, downloading pirated software is illegal and can infect your PC with malware, and that last bit is doubly true in the dubious AI era we now live in. For now, the only thing to do is observe and report. Here's where things stand with GTA 6 PC ports. Is GTA 6 fully playable on PC? No, but it's getting closer. Several projects have made it as rendering and playing early portions of the game at low framerates (10-16 fps average), but it's hard to verify clips making the rounds when so many are obvious fakes . title: Marathon's new runner shell is a jet-propelled robot samurai who wants to hurt you
summary: Sounds great!
body: We're just a couple weeks away from Marathon's Symbiosis update , a hefty overhaul patch that's aiming to inject some juice into the shooter's live service appeal with the addition of PvE roguelite and Team Deathmatch modes, new weapons, and even a social hub for hanging out with fellow runners and testing guns at the firing range. And that's all great. But today, Bungie dropped a new cinematic that presents its strongest argument for why Symbiosis should have our attention: You can play as a terrifying, sports-car scarlet robot samurai with a sword arm and jet legs. While Bungie previously revealed Bishop, the new runner shell arriving with Symbiosis, in the update's first gameplay trailer earlier this month, the new cinematic provides a strong sense of the power fantasy it's trying to capture. By which I mean Bungie clearly wants you to feel like a nightmarish apex predator. Like a xenomorph if a xenomorph was bright red and had cool space guns. title: GTA 6 recomp leaders bail out as Take-Two cracks down on illicit efforts to get the game running on PC
summary: The leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recreate GTA 6 on PC, have quit the project, although others are still trying to carry it on.
body: Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar. The release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, said on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." In a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead quickly. But then things began moving quickly in a different direction. "I quit guys…

title: Mass Effect writer says 'as a fan I would have been happy with the solution' they came up with for ME3's endings in ME Universe
summary: My personal solution would be playable elcor main character. Can't go wrong with that.
body: Spoilers for the end of Mass Effect 3 follow, naturally. You know what? I didn't have many questions left at the end of Mass Effect 3. Joker was a robot now. His robot girlfriend was perhaps less of a robot? Shepard converted herself into a dotfile to make the Reapers chill out, and Buzz Aldrin's talents lie in areas other than voice acting. I had plenty of questions when BioWare announced Mass Effect 5 was gonna be a thing though. Could you really write a Mass Effect story in the radically changed galaxy we were left with at the end of Shepard's adventure? Apparently, you could. In a recent AMA on Reddit (via IGN ), BioWare writer Cat Valente wrote that the now-cancelled Mass Effect sequel's team put a lot of work into handling ME3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off, [or] at least not piss them off completely". The goal, says Valente, was to write a continuation of Mass Effect's narrative that "wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another". That tracks with what we've heard before: leaks have suggested ME5 was set to more or less wrap all the previous game's endings into one (Deus Ex: Invisible War style, hell yeah). title: Steam revamps its marketplace for the 2nd time this year
summary: Big news for the skin barons in your life.
body: If you're normal, you probably never think about the Steam community market. If you're like me, you only touch it to sell the mountains of trading cards you get from idling . If you're a true lunatic, you're running a roaring trade in Counter-Strike 2 skins and are either unfathomably rich or trapped in a life of penury. Either way, some news: Valve has been tinkering at the Steam marketplace again, and in an update yesterday announced a rebuilt market home page that's slightly more pleasant to handle and look at, while being more personalised to the games you're actually playing. This is in addition to a set of changes to the market Valve released (in beta) back in May . The new market home is, says Valve, faster to load up, but it's not just a new gloss of paint. It's swapped out the pre-update Popular Items section—which mostly just showed a list of CS2 crates—for new Trending Items lists that show the popular market items for games you've actually been playing. When I look at it, I see Path of Exile, Warframe, Crisis In The Kremlin, and, uh, Dota 2. I've never touched Dota 2 in my life, so not sure what's happening there, but you get the idea. title: Trump claims credit for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, posts meme depicting Huang holding up a bra victoriously
summary: US politicians on both sides of the aisle are reeling.
body: US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he personally "convinced" the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang . Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO a little under two weeks ago after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (no relation), who formerly controlled Singaporean tech company Megaspeed International and has been the subject of US national security concerns related to AI chip exports to China. Following the admission, as well as reports of two other affairs with Nvidia employees, Huang resigned as Nvidia president, CEO, and board member. Last week, amid calls for Huang's return from tech CEOs and investors, the Nvidia board said firmly that it would not reinstate him. Cue the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia title card: The gang reinstated him. On Monday, the Nvidia board said that it had "voted unanimously" to bring Huang back after receiving "input from senior levels of the United States government." Nvidia shares shot up 31.48% during Monday's trading. Trump has taken credit for the change of heart. "I made the deal," he told CNBC. The President also posted a congratulatory AI-generated image depicting Huang as himself surviving an attempted assassinat…

title: 2026 Steam Awards pit the GOTY winners of the past 10 years against each other in an all-out battle for supremacy
summary: It's the 10th anniversary of the Steam Awards and that means it's time for something new.
body: The festive month of December is rapidly bearing down on us and you know what that means: It's time for another round of the Steam Awards, the annual exercise in which we hand out awards to our favorite games on Steam, hence the name. First, though, comes the nomination process , which kicked off today and will run until November 30. This year's event is a little different from those of years past, because 2026 is the 10th anniversary of the Steam Awards. To mark the big birthday, Valve has added a few new categories inspired by previous years: Just Five More Minutes Defies Description This is My Job Now For even bigger excitement, there's also a new "Hall of Fame" category that pits the Game of the Year winners from the previous decade against one another in a final fight for supremacy. title: This fan-made map shows why Queen's Domain is the true GOTY, and you can even upload your save to it to track the things you have left to find
summary: Cartographic miracles.
body: The world wants me to write more about Grand Theft Auto 6 and I bravely answer "No". Last week, I obtained 50% of the endings available in Queen's Domain, the best videogame to release in the year 2026. The next 50% require, well, a lot of nook-scouring and cranny-uncovering—many more hours of gameplay which I am preserving for myself as a Christmas holiday treat. And when I do, I suspect I might make a little (just a little) use of this rad Queen's Domain map by a creator called Leny15 . Barely a week ago I wrote that "I suspect a cross-section of [Queen's Domain's] goliath, entwined map would make for a killer bit of wall art". Well, I was right. Here it is and it looks rad as hell. No, really. Even if you're not a Queen's Domain player—or maybe especially if you're not—take a look at this thing. It's one thing to wander these maps as a player, it's another to get a totally flexible birdseye view of how dense, twisty and interconnected they are. I will never stop being blown away by how knotty and elaborate this game is; I love it. I will also never believe I have actually explored all of it. I'll be honest, gang, I really feel like I've plumbed the depths of this game, but this…
